exposure: Child-Mother Index (newborn weight divided by squared maternal height)
cohort: 47,007 singleton births in Denmark in 2009 with a gestational age between 37+0 and 41+6 weeks.
finding: A Child-Mother Index above 14.1 hg/m2 was associated with an increased risk of third- and fourth-degree perineal tears, nonelective cesarean delivery, and instrumental procedures.
